items.rationale: Theft damage to the frame is covered under 2.3.1(b), with replacement limited to the pre-loss grade under 7.1.9. The €245 gross estimate is reduced by the shared €500 mobility cap under 4.2.2, using an estimated factor of 500/919.
The brakes sustained theft damage, so like-for-like parts are covered under 7.1.7(b). The €139 gross estimate is prorated by 500/919 under 4.2.2.
The tracker helped locate the bicycle, but no separate loss or damage to it is established. Sections 3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude its replacement on these facts.
Routine servicing is excluded under 3.1.6, and the second bicycle was unaffected under 7.1.5.
Neither accessory is identified as stolen or damaged. Sections 3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude new accessories supplied in connection with the claim.
Necessary carriage of replacement parts is covered under 7.1.7(f), but shipping for the elective purchases is not. If attributable to the covered repair, €25 gross is prorated by 500/919.

Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.10 require a necessary attendance attributable to covered work, which this generic line does not establish. If a separate €25 attendance is substantiated, the revised cap factor is 500/944.
Fitting and aligning the replacement frame and brakes is covered under 7.1.7(c), provided it does not duplicate separately billed labour. The €140 gross estimate is prorated by 500/919.
Section 7.1.7(e) allows sundries consumed in the theft repair, subject to allocation under 7.1.10. If the €7 gross charge is for covered repair materials, it is prorated by 500/919.
Section 7.1.7(d) covers apprentice labour actually used on the theft repair; 7.1.8(g) excludes any time already included in assembly. One distinct hour at €18 gross is prorated by 500/919.
Skilled labour is covered under 7.1.7(d) if attributable to the theft repair and not already billed as assembly. One distinct hour at €38 gross is prorated by 500/919.
The initial locksmith attendance was necessary to release the bicycle and is separately covered under 5.2.2(a). The €32 gross estimate is prorated by 500/919 under the mobility cap.
Section 5.2.2(b) expressly covers cutting and removing the lock to release the recovered bicycle. The €100 gross estimate for the whole line is prorated by 500/919.

Sections 5.2.2(a) and 7.1.8(f) allow a second attendance only if it was necessary; the account establishes only the initial visit. If a distinct €30 return visit is substantiated, the revised cap factor is 500/949.

items.description: Mandatory impound release and storage fee
items.rationale: The yard required payment before releasing the bicycle, so the fee is covered under 5.2.2(c), not excluded as administration. €100 plus 19% VAT is €119 gross; the recovery subtotal is below €1,000, but the shared mobility cap prorates this line by 500/919.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d) expressly exclude claim-processing charges. This is separate from the yard's mandatory release fee.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers all labour grades used for lock removal, but 7.1.8(g) bars any time already included in the cutting charge. One distinct hour at €18 gross is prorated by 500/919.
Skilled recovery labour is covered under 5.2.2(b) to the extent it does not duplicate the cutting charge. One distinct hour at €38 gross is prorated by 500/919.
